name: Play SMS and Call Log permission policy
plain: Apps can read SMS or call logs only if they are the default handler or qualify for a narrow exception.
meaning: Since 9 March 2019 Google limits these permissions to default SMS, Phone or Assistant apps and a few declared exceptions. It stops mass harvesting for contact lists and ads.

android.store_policy: Permissions Declaration Form required; default handler or approved exception; data may not be sold
android.api_surface: Play Console > App content > Sensitive permissions
android.note: Alternatives: SMS Retriever and User Consent APIs for OTP.

ios.note: iOS has no readable SMS or call log. Message Filter extensions see unknown senders only.

limits.headline: Can't see your texts or call history unless it is your default texting or phone app
limits.user_action: You set the app as your default SMS or Phone app, or enter a one time code yourself
can: Handle your texts if you made it the default SMS app
Auto fill a one time code using the SMS Retriever or User Consent
Use the call log if it is the default Phone or Assistant app, or a declared exception
cannot: Collect texts for contact lists or ads
See your texts on iPhone; it has no way in
Get call history without a Play approved reason
See any texts on iPhone beyond unknown senders, even with a message filter
limits.differs: Android allows it for default apps and few exceptions. iPhone has no way in, apart from message filters for unknown senders.

story.what_it_is: Google's rule that only default phone or text apps may read your texts and call history.

marketing.name: SMS and Call Log permissions policy
marketing.pitch: Only default SMS, Phone or Assistant apps, plus a few approved exceptions, may use these permissions.

story.for_you: Your text messages and call history stay private from random apps. An app can only read them if you make it your default texting or phone app.
story.for_makers: Apps used to harvest messages for loans scoring or contact lists. Now makers use narrow tools such as the SMS Retriever to read one login code, or ask the person to type it.

use_cases.example: A texting app becomes your default so it can read and send your texts.
A bank uses SMS Retriever to read a single one time code with no broad permission.
A game that sends a verification code reads only that code through the retriever tool.
Shady loan apps used to scrape contacts and texts to pressure borrowers, which led to the rule.
A call blocker app becomes the default call screening app to see incoming numbers.
A backup app asks for a special exception to copy texts, with a clear reason.

story.android_note: Since 9 March 2019 Play limits these permissions to default handlers and a few exceptions.
story.ios_note: iOS never lets apps read texts or call logs. Messages filter extensions only classify unknown senders.

history.change: SMS and Call Log restrictions effective 9 March 2019
